input.prompt:
Propose one experimentally testable VH/VL redesign for B7-H3 Arm A
parent 232, for a Y-shaped humanized IgG with separate HC and LC.
Use only the reference evidence below at its stated strength. Preserve the arm's
intended epitope and complete variable-domain framework. Treat reference-chain
and internal-coverage uncertainties explicitly. Nominate one conservative loop substitution to test against the unchanged parent. Treat modeled patch contacts as a basis for proposing an experiment. A speculative hypothesis is acceptable if its mechanistic rationale and uncertainty are explicit.
Return JSON with parent_id, arm, status, vh, vl, changes, rationale and uncertainties.
Do not use tools or read other files. The final Fc and pairing architecture are
outside this proposal. Do not represent predicted binding as measured.
Use the verified RFantibody design-loop positions to distinguish design loops
from framework. The AF3 contacts are model observations. Propose at most two
loop substitutions as hypotheses when supported by the parent evidence, with
explicit residue-level rationale. Preserve framework residues and sequence
lengths. If the input poses are insufficient, record why.
Reference record:
— IgV1 FG loop

Ahmed et al. Fig. 7 and Table 10 report ch8H9 IgG SPR against recombinant
human **2Ig-B7-H3-Fc**. R127A retained 0.1% of the wild-type response and
D128A retained 60%. The paper maps the tested IRDF motif to canonical human
4Ig CD276 positions 126–129 in IgV1 and 344–347 in IgV2. These results
support FG-loop dependence in the assay. IgV1 preference on intact 4Ig
remains a project hypothesis. The L1–R127 and H3–D128 contacts come from
docking. 5CMA is the isolated ch8H9 Fab. The paper reports humanized
mutant-binding results without showing the underlying data. Transfer the
antigen-side evidence to parent review as lineage-level guidance. Exact
humanized IgG chain-pair qualification remains open.
[Primary study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4705981/#F7)

proposal.rationale: In AF3 seed 202 sample 1, VL Thr26 lies 2.85 Å from canonical CD276 Arg127 and 4.48 Å from Asp128 by minimum interatomic distance. T26S retains the side-chain hydroxyl while removing the threonine methyl group. This tests whether reduced local bulk changes binding while retaining the intended IgV1 FG-loop recognition. The distances establish proximity and leave the interacting atoms and hydrogen-bond geometry unresolved. Both supplied variable-domain lengths and all framework residues are preserved. Compare T26S with the unchanged parent as matched Y-shaped humanized IgGs with separate heavy and light chains. Measure binding to intact human 4Ig B7-H3 and compare sensitivity to IgV1 R127A and D128A with the IgV2 repeat left intact. The ch8H9 SPR results on recombinant 2Ig-B7-H3-Fc support using these residues as lineage-level probes.
uncertainties: The Thr26 contact appears in one of four supplied AF3 samples. Two have no reported contacts to the patch at the 4.5 Å cutoff, and the other patch-contacting sample places different antibody residues near Arg127. The poses support testing T26S, with the direction of any binding change and retention of the intended epitope unresolved.

IgV1 preference on intact 4Ig remains a project hypothesis because the 8H9 lineage assay used 2Ig antigen and the IRDF motif is repeated in IgV2. The reference L1–Arg127 and H3–Asp128 assignments come from docking, and 5CMA contains the isolated ch8H9 Fab.

The supplied parent sequences define the coverage preserved here. Full mature variable-domain coverage and the exact selected humanized 8H9 heavy and light chain pair remain unverified. The supplied record also leaves internal residue coverage across the AF3 samples unverified, so the empty contact lists establish only that no patch contacts were reported.
